//: VOTES (docs/events/votes.md): the Senate's votes and the elections, before, during and after. The ladder's and the consuls' reports are of the Republic only (era imperium absent); the reports of the Senate's floor come in either era, since the chamber sits under the Imperium too. They read the marks VoteMarks writes: moves_a_motion, moves_against_you and undecided_on_yours on the docket, my_motion_open; voted_with_you and voted_against_you at the count of the player's motion; abstention_noticed with noticed_your_abstention; bribe_out with took_your_purse; act_went_against_houses with act_went_against_them; beat_yours_at_the_count and lost_to_yours_at_the_count at the ladder's count; and the engine's own motion_open, motion_passed_mine, motion_against_me, election_held, consul_elected, ladder_election_held, standing_for_office, office:consul_*, trust_is_low, public_trust. Threads: owes_you_a_vote, made a favour owed each way at the next session by VoteMarks.Bargains, and promised_your_vote, made one owed by your house (a_vote_for_a_vote, a_bought_vote_called_in); bought_your_vote (a_vote_for_a_vote, then a_bought_vote_called_in); grudge_against_you (those_who_voted_against_you, then an_old_grudge_against_your_motion or an_old_grudge_on_the_docket); lost_at_the_count (the one of yours who lost, for the_one_who_won_the_office); dined_with_you (the_consul_elects_feast: the consul once lets a motion of yours stand that they would veto); pamphlet_war (a_smear_after_the_election, then the_pamphlet_scandal); met_as_colleague (your_colleague_the_consul, once a colleague).

effects.text: {self.name} gave {senator.name} of {senator.house} a vote for a vote. Each house owes the other one now, and the chamber will see whether both are paid.
{self.name} let {senator.name} of {senator.house} pay for the house's vote. It was quietly done, and not quite quietly enough.
{self.name} told {senator.name} of {senator.house} that the house's vote was not for trade.
{self.name} told {buyer.name} of {buyer.house} the house would vote with them again, unpaid this time. They will be watching the count.
{self.name} sent {buyer.name} of {buyer.house} back the price of the house's vote, with something over. The bargain is ended, in front of witnesses.
{self.name} told {buyer.name} of {buyer.house} that one vote had been sold and no more. {buyer.name} made sure the chamber heard about the one.
{self.name} went to {doubter.name} of {doubter.house} and spent an evening on the motion. It was an evening well spent, or so it seemed at the door.
{self.name} had {doubter.name} of {doubter.house} to dinner. The motion was not mentioned once, which was the point.
{self.name} spoke for the motion in the chamber. {doubter.name} of {doubter.house} was seen to listen.
{self.name} let {doubter.name} of {doubter.house} make up their own mind on the motion.
{self.name} told {leader.name} of {leader.house} that the house's silence on the vote had been a matter of conscience. It was believed, and not liked.
{self.name} promised {leader.name} of {leader.house} that the house would be on its feet at the next vote.
{self.name} sent a gift to {leader.house} the day after the vote, and nothing was said about the empty seat.
{self.name} told {leader.name} of {leader.house} that the house's vote was its own to cast or keep. The bench heard about it by evening.
{self.name} gave a dinner for the houses that carried the motion, with {ally.name} of {ally.house} at the right hand.
{ally.name} of {ally.house} gave the dinner for the motion that carried, and {self.name} went as a guest and let them have the evening. The city said it had been their motion.
{self.name} thanked the houses that carried the motion by letter. {ally.name} of {ally.house} had hoped for more than a letter.
{self.name} went to {loser.name} of {loser.house} after the vote with an offer for their trouble. Nobody lost twice that day.
{self.name} let {loser.name} of {loser.house} lose the vote and said nothing to them. They have not forgotten it.
{self.name} reminded the Senate, from the floor, which house had lost. {loser.name} of {loser.house} sat through it.
{self.name} answered {rival.name} of {rival.house} on the floor and named the old quarrel that the motion was really about. The chamber knows now what it is voting on.
{self.name} went to {rival.name} of {rival.house} and made peace over the old vote. The motion stands; what comes after it may not.
{self.name} let {rival.name} of {rival.house} have their day in the chamber, and kept the grudge where it was.
{self.name} sent {rival.name} of {rival.house} six hundred credits' worth of reasons to let the old quarrel go before the vote. They took them.
{self.name} rose before the vote and said what {rival.name} of {rival.house} was really voting on: an old quarrel, not the motion. The chamber heard it, and the quarrel is out in the open now.
{self.name} let {rival.name} of {rival.house} speak against the motion in every corridor, and answered none of it. The grudge was spent on that vote.
{self.name} promised {friend.name} of {friend.house} to move the repeal of the Act when the chamber would hear it.
{self.name} sent {friend.name} of {friend.house} what it would take to carry the Act's cost through the year, and asked nothing for it.
{self.name} wrote back to {friend.name} of {friend.house} that the law was the law, for every house alike. It was the right answer, and it was received as one.
{self.name} stood up in the Senate and said that the purse had been the house's doing and not {bought.name}'s. It cost the house more, and {bought.house} will not forget it.
{self.name} paid {bought.name} of {bought.house} for what the bought vote had cost them on the floor.
{self.name} let it be said that {bought.name} of {bought.house} had named the price. Half the chamber believed it. {bought.name} did not have to.
{self.name} walked the wards with {kin.name} for a month before the count. They learned more of the city in that month than in a year of speeches.
{self.name} taught {kin.name} how a crowd is won and how it is lost. They will speak better at the count for it.
{self.name} told {kin.name} that an office is won by the one who stands for it.
{self.name} opened the house's accounts to the praetors, against what {accuser.name} of {accuser.house} was saying in the squares. The magistrates are a little better believed for it.
{self.name} paid a pamphleteer to say what was known of the canvass of {accuser.name} of {accuser.house}. Their pamphleteer answered by the end of the week.
{self.name} let what {accuser.name} of {accuser.house} was saying about the count blow over. It took longer than it should have.
{self.name} called off the house's pamphleteer, and {accuser.name} of {accuser.house} called off theirs. The squares found something else to read.
{self.name} had the pamphlets of {accuser.name} of {accuser.house} brought before a praetor. They stopped. The quarrel did not.
{self.name} let the pamphleteers go on until they tired of it. Neither house came out of it well, and {accuser.name}'s came out worse. The Reach trusted its magistrates the less for it.
{self.name} went to congratulate {victor.name} of {victor.house} on the Senate steps, where the city could see it done. {kin.name} saw it done too.
{self.name} had the count read again for {kin.name}. It stood, as counts do. The house was seen to fight for its own, and {victor.name} of {victor.house} was seen to be doubted.
{self.name} said nothing about the count. {victor.name} of {victor.house} took up the office.
{self.name} sent the house's people to keep the peace at the booths on the day of the count. The commons noticed who came, and who did not.
{self.name} spoke to the crowd from the Senate steps until it went home. It was not a speech anyone would quote, and it worked.
{self.name} told the lictors to clear the squares. They were cleared. The commons will remember whose word it was.
{self.name} barred the house's doors on the day of the count and waited for the noise to stop.
{self.name} dined with the Senate at the table of {grandee.name} of {grandee.house}, Senior Consul, and was seen there.
{self.name} sent a gift ahead to the table of {grandee.name} of {grandee.house}, and the table talked about it.
{self.name} asked across the table of {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} what the consulship would do for the house's bench. It was a fair question, asked at the wrong time.
{self.name} did not go to the table of {grandee.name} of {grandee.house}. The empty chair was counted.
{self.name} and {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} divided the consulship's business between them, and kept to it.
{self.name} told {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} that the senior chair led the consulship. {grandee.name} agreed, and did not like it.
{self.name} kept their own counsel with {grandee.name} of {grandee.house}, and watched, and learned a good deal about how {grandee.name} works.
